To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the fluorescence of PSII is not significantly affected by crystallization.

picosecond fluorescence kinetics of PSII in the open state is not affected by the crystal state or replacement of Ca(2+) in OEC by Sr(2+) and that the fluorescence kinetics is affected by electron acceptors and transport inhibitors.
the picosecond kinetics of fluorescence of PSII in the crystals is indistinguishable from the fluorescence of PSII isolated from the cyanobacterium T. elongatus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the oxygen evolving complex and the mechanism of water oxidation.
the comparison of the fluorescence kinetics of PSII core particles in the crystalline and solubilized states, and of PSII in the native and Sr(2+) biosynthetically replaced state.
the structure and function of PSII, and how these are affected by the presence of different metal ions in the OEC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

picosecond fluorescence decay kinetics is a sensitive probe for the structural integrity of PSII reaction centres and that the fluorescence decay of the crystals is a good model for the decay of solubilized PSII.
the crystal structure is a valid model for the solubilized PSII core particle.
PSII crystals are a useful model for studying the function of PSII in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the picosecond kinetics of the PSII crystals are very similar to the kinetics of the solubilisised PSII.
PSII crystals are suitable for studying light-induced processes.
the crystal structure is a good model of the solubile PSII complex.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the fluorescence of PSII core complexes and PSII crystals can be used to monitor structural differences in the reaction centre.
the picosecond time-resolved fluorescence of PSII core particles is not affected by crystallisation.
PSII crystals are a useful model system for studying the structure and function of the OEC, but that the crystal structure is not necessarily identical to the structure in the solubilized complex.
